IEEE SSCS Code-a-Chip / ISSCC 2027

Comparator Atlas

Wei-Lun Hsu — National Tsing Hua University

SKY130 StrongARM comparator: calibrated schematic characterization and archived nominal-layout simulations. Decision correctness, delay and core-rail energy are reported for explicit input, PVT and deadline conditions.

Study design and aggregate schematic results

The schematic study uses ngspice 47 and 49 × 2 declared operating cases: 45 PVT combinations plus four nominal stress controls per design. The selected circuit contains 27 transistor instances, including physical trim branches.

With the same local calibration, a 1 ns deadline and sampled |input| ≥ 1 mV, correct-point coverage changes from 79.1% to 94.9%. Mean core-rail energy changes by +75.9% over 392 matched points; this excludes external drivers and calibration infrastructure.

Selected circuit: lvt_balanced_4b.

The transistor gate-area proxy is 1.90x the original. Matched mean core-rail energy is 143.01 → 251.53 fJ/cycle. This is not a claim of lower area, lower system power, silicon yield or a new comparator topology.

The comparison uses the same local calibration policy, input band and deadline. A lower-energy candidate is included to show the accuracy-energy tradeoff.

The PVT comparison is schematic-level. The physical-layout section separately reports nominal code-zero measurements and the remaining slow-corner limitation.

27-device circuit topology and trim branches

The source-checked MOS schematic shows the cross-coupled core, a reset PFET repeated at the four listed nodes, and one trim bit repeated on both sides for k = 0–3. Filled dots are electrical junctions; unmarked crossings are unconnected. Matching node labels across panels denote the same net. All 27 instances, device flavors and body ties are retained. Vector PDF schematic.

Nine-candidate selection on three declared conditions

Selection used TT/1.8 V/27 C, SS/1.62 V/-40 C and FF/1.95 V/125 C, six declared input values, and 2x energy / 4x gate-area-proxy budgets. The initial prototype informed the family. The recorded objective and candidate list were frozen before this campaign. No global optimum is asserted.

Source record

Calibration deadline and scored input band

The hardware comparison uses the same local 3.5 ns calibration policy. The 1 ns policy is a separate ablation: it minimizes the finite-deadline decision interval rather than only its long-deadline offset. A failed calibration is explicitly unavailable, not silently replaced by code zero.

Retained cold-corner schematic waveform

This condition was known to be weak in the first prototype and was included in selection. It illustrates mechanism; the reserved/full PVT tables, not this one waveform, support generalization within the declared grid.

Input history, settling and interface perturbations

Five nominal/extreme PVT conditions, four inputs, and eight explicitly defined stresses per design. Codes are frozen before perturbing the interface. The history step changes the external input at 18 to 18.05 ns; evaluation starts at 22.025 ns. Pin error includes deterministic settling and kickback, not random noise.

Selected design at all 49 conditions for +/-1 mV and both local policies; baseline at five extreme/nominal conditions; additionally every validation run with an output decision margin within 5 mV of a rail threshold. All six reporting deadlines are checked. Initially sensitive points are subsequently refined under the recorded halving policy. Refinement limits are identical outcomes, at most 1% core-energy difference and at most 20 ps resolved-latency difference. These checks are not production signoff.

Layout geometry, structural checks and five-condition pilot

The nominal 27-device layout has recorded GDS, named-style DRC, independent LVS, wrong-net/bulk/width/SVT-LVT negative controls, and separate connectivity/C/RC exports. The original layout development used five code-zero conditions. The following expanded study covers 45 PVT conditions with the same nominal geometry. Neither is a post-layout reproduction of the calibrated width-stress study.

The compact predecessor failed M2 pad-notch spacing and was never simulated. Four M2 bridges repair it without changing devices, pins or the other mask geometry. Archived-deck differences are measured against the prior legal balanced layout, not attributed to the bridges alone. Listed capacitance is a sum of emitted elements, not an effective impedance.

Recorded verification run: compact-layout repair evidence. The workflow's failure status reflects the preserved 1 ns performance gate, not a hidden DRC/LVS failure. Source replay instructions bind the original experimental commit.

Nominal 45-PVT grid: 180 SC and 180 archived RC points

The repaired nominal, code-zero schematic and RC circuits were evaluated at five process corners, three supplies and three temperatures: 45 conditions, four signed inputs each, 180 points per mode. The primary 2 ns deadline was declared before this expanded study; 1 ns is reported alongside it.

Archived RC decks: 180/180 correct at 2 ns; 156/180 at 1 ns. The other 24 points are late, with no wrong decisions. All point histories meet the same numerical criteria at 10 and 5 ps.

Each cell is the maximum sampled delay over -10, -3, +3 and +10 mV. Black outlines mark a missed 1 ns sample. Five conditions had been observed in the earlier pilot; forty are new post-layout conditions, not a blinded external test.

implementation points correct_at_1ns correct_at_2ns mean_core_energy_fj mean_delay_ns_at_2ns worst_delay_ns_at_2ns
Schematic 180 180 180 245.8 0.3033 0.738
Extracted RC 180 156 180 425.5 0.7076 1.835

The slowest sampled RC point is FS / 1.62 V / -40 C / -3 mV: 1.835 ns. Mean core energy is 245.84 fJ schematic versus 425.49 fJ RC. The mean per-point overhead is 73.45%; the ratio of population means is 73.08%.

Both modes in this study use ngspice 47, the same pinned SKY130 models, nominal dimensions, code zero, 5 fF output loads, 0.5 VDD common mode and a 10 ns clock with 50 ps edges. This is a finite sampled result, not a noise, mismatch-yield or continuous-input guarantee. It does not retroactively change the earlier 1 ns pilot.

Scope: RC timing and energy are results of the archived simulation decks; extracted-model physical fidelity remains unqualified. RC-versus-C differences are not isolated resistance effects or silicon predictions. Extraction-model evidence and limitations.

Publication-size vector figures: PVT timing, paired comparison, worst-case waveform.

Reproduction, scope and references

Public entry: Comparator_Atlas.ipynb, with Python 3.10 review mode and Colab bootstrap. Optional Windows bootstrap: node scripts\setup.mjs. Then run the CLI stages optimize, study, stress and report with the project Python and -m comparator_atlas.

Full commands, tool versions and source-data locations are in REPRODUCIBILITY.md. Saved outputs are checked against their source records before analysis.

Scope

These are deterministic simulations. Controlled width perturbations are not a foundry mismatch distribution or yield. Core energy excludes external drivers and calibration infrastructure. The calibrated schematic and nominal-layout experiments have separate condition sets; DRC/LVS do not establish silicon performance or complete foundry signoff.

Established ideas and related work

  • B. Razavi, The StrongARM Latch, 2015.
  • S. Li, Z. Xu and T. Iizuka, Analysis of strong-arm comparator with auxiliary pair for offset calibration, 2022.
  • Open comparator optimization research and an existing SKY130/LVT comparator example. Their code, figures, performance claims and statistical assumptions are not reused as this study's evidence.
  • Official SKY130 primitive models and current competition rules.
